name: Amṛtacandra Sūri
dates_notes: Usually placed in the late tenth century from the chronology of the Kundakunda commentarial tradition. Details of his life are not independently secure.
core_thesis: Amṛtacandra gives the Digambara Adhyātma tradition a durable philosophical and ethical form through his commentaries on Kundakunda and his independent verse treatise. He clarifies the relation between the conventional and ultimate standpoints without treating moral discipline as dispensable, and relates the analysis of karma to a program of internal transformation.

engaged_works.title: Atmakhyati
engaged_works.ascription_notes: Securely transmitted as Amṛtacandra's commentary on Kundakunda's *Samayasāra*.
engaged_works.summary: A major Sanskrit commentary on the *Samayasāra*, explaining the distinction between the conventional and ultimate standpoints and the self's relation to karmic bondage.

engaged_works.title: Purusarthasiddhyupaya
engaged_works.ascription_notes: Securely ascribed in the Digambara tradition; the Sanskrit text survives in editions and translations.
engaged_works.summary: An independent verse treatise on the path to liberation, integrating the analysis of intention, violence, karmic influx, restraint, and ethical practice within the Digambara Adhyātma framework.
